stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Top chipmakers embrace ASML’s $400M machines, agree to crucial chipmaking change
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Major chipmakers are adopting new ASML equipment.
The industry has agreed to a significant change in chip manufacturing processes.
This procedural change is projected to increase the productivity of the new ASML machines by 40%.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a modern LLM release.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is being used for text generation tasks.
Categorizes the model within the broader ecosystem of transformers and LLMs.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to run locally on user hardware, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: ChatGPT Sketch turns your bad drawings into detailed AI images
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI introduced a new feature called 'Sketch' within ChatGPT Images 2.5.
Users can now generate detailed AI images by providing a simple doodle or sketch as input.
This integration allows for a more intuitive, drawing-based method of prompting image generation.

stories.title: Meta bets on AI agent Muse to catch up in AI race
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Meta is heavily investing in Muse, a new personal AI assistant, as part of a major strategic shift.
The initiative is aimed at significantly improving Meta's competitive standing in the rapidly evolving AI landscape.
Muse is positioned as a tool designed to make advanced AI accessible to a broad consumer base.

stories.title: “This is the AI men actually use”: Meta ads pushed apps nudifying real teens
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Meta is facing scrutiny for allowing ads that promote body image issues on Instagram, specifically targeting young girls.
The issue involves ads that 'nudify' or alter young users' photos, raising significant concerns about digital body image and mental health.
The company was criticized for delaying the removal of these problematic advertisements.

stories.title: When LLM Decompilers Recompile More and Preserve Less
stories.author: Kristopher Micinski
bullet_points: LLM-based decompilers are emerging as a new paradigm for recovering high-level source code from machine code.
Unlike traditional tools (e.g., Ghidra), LLM decompilers generate clean, idiomatic C code.
The primary evaluation metric for these new LLM decompilers is their ability to be successfully recompiled and re-executed.

stories.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
stories.author: Szymon Rusinkiewicz
bullet_points: UniMate is a unified foundation model designed to synthesize articulated motion for diverse, arbitrary skeletons.
It overcomes limitations of existing learned animators which are often topology-constrained or require extensive fine-tuning.
The model allows motion generation directly from a rigged 3D asset and a text prompt without needing test-time optimization.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: AI power users claim Anthropic duped them with subscriptions, and they’re taking it to court
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: Anthropic is facing a class action lawsuit from AI power users.
The core complaint is that Anthropic misled subscribers about the value of its top-tier pricing.
The dispute arises despite Anthropic claiming power users are central to its business strategy.

stories.title: Tesla Cybercab doesn’t have any manual controls — but it does have a virtual joystick
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla Cybercab is designed without traditional manual controls like a steering wheel or pedals.
Initial reports suggested the vehicle was entirely autonomous.
Riders have since discovered a 'secret' virtual joystick allowing for some manual input.

stories.title: Google complies with EU rules for travel searches, says the new results stink
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is complying with new European Union regulations concerning travel search results.
The implementation of these EU rules has reportedly led to a degradation in the quality of Google's search results.
The story highlights ongoing regulatory scrutiny by the EU regarding Google's alleged anticompetitive search practices.

stories.title: EV batteries last longer than drivers feared
stories.author: Kana Inagaki and Clara Murray, Financial Times
bullet_points: Study indicates EV batteries maintain high usability after significant mileage.
Used electric vehicles can retain approximately 90% of original battery capacity.
This retention rate is observed after driving 150,000 kilometers.

stories.title: RegionFed: Federated Learning for Personalized Query Understanding in Heterogeneous Retail Environments
stories.author: Chittaranjan Tripathy
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of data heterogeneity in retail search systems across different geographic regions.
Proposes 'RegionFed,' a Federated Learning approach designed to handle personalized query understanding while maintaining privacy.
Overcomes limitations of standard FL (global model sacrifice) and existing personalized FL methods (parameter-level collapse).

stories.title: A Deep Generative Model for Synthesizing Labeled Wireless Signals
stories.author: Yuan Shen
bullet_points: Proposes a deep generative model to synthesize labeled wireless signals.
Addresses the high cost and difficulty of acquiring real-world, labeled wireless sensing datasets.
Overcomes limitations of traditional synthesis methods, which rely on environmental models and require extensive tuning.

stories.title: Multi-Step Tool-Calling over Korean Open Public APIs: A Benchmark and a Data-Synthesis Recipe
stories.author: Kyuseong Lim
bullet_points: Introduces KOPA-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test multi-step tool-calling capabilities using real-world Korean government APIs.
Addresses a critical industry challenge: the performance gap of open-source LLMs when required to chain multiple tool-calls under data-sovereignty constraints.
Presents EDGE, a novel data synthesis recipe utilizing an Execution-grounded Dynamic Graph to improve evaluation and training for this specific task.

stories.title: Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence
stories.author: Houssem Chatbri
bullet_points: The research evaluates the quality of Large Language Model (LLM) explanations by testing two criteria: necessity and sufficiency.
The study addresses the assumption that LLM explanations align with the model's actual, observable decision-making behavior in agent workflows.
This work is relevant for operators who use LLM outputs for monitoring, error diagnosis, or escalation decisions.

stories.title: Reflection-aware Generative Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Tae-Hyun Oh
bullet_points: Introduces Ref-GeNVS, a training-free method for generative novel view synthesis (NVS) specifically designed for mirror scenes.
Addresses a limitation in existing diffusion models where they fail to recognize and utilize reflected content in mirror environments.
The core technique involves estimating the mirror plane and generating virtual views by reflecting camera poses from input images.

stories.title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models
stories.author: Christian Feiler
bullet_points: The paper investigates a critical flaw in evaluating LLMs used for molecular property prediction: the inability to distinguish between true prediction and verbatim retrieval of published data.
Auditing 22 frontier models across 12 benchmarks revealed that verbatim retrieval is a widespread phenomenon, occurring in over 50% of models on five specific datasets.
The findings suggest that while retrieval is common, its prevalence is highly dependent on the specific benchmark dataset being used.

stories.title: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
stories.author: Yanfeng Wang
bullet_points: CUA-Universe introduces a scalable and dynamic environment designed for hybrid AI agents.
It addresses the limitation of current computer-use agents, which often rely too heavily on inefficient GUI interactions.
The environment supports the necessary coordination between visual (GUI) and precise command-line (CLI) operations over shared application state.

stories.title: RegionFed: Federated Learning for Personalized Query Understanding in Heterogeneous Retail Environments
stories.author: Chittaranjan Tripathy
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of data heterogeneity in retail search systems across different geographic regions.
Proposes 'RegionFed,' a Federated Learning approach designed to enable personalized query understanding.
Overcomes limitations of standard FL (global models sacrificing regional performance) and existing parameter-level personalized FL methods.

stories.title: Distill Globally, Adapt Locally: Reasoning Distillation and Product-Type Test-Time Training for Scalable Trade-Up Recommendation
stories.author: Amin Banitalebi-Dehkordi
bullet_points: Addresses the computational impracticality of applying large language models (LLMs) directly to massive product recommendation datasets.
Proposes a two-level framework involving 'Reasoning Distillation' to transfer LLM reasoning into an efficient, non-generative student model.
Introduces 'Product-Type Test-Time Training' to adapt the model's decision boundary to specific trade-up criteria.

stories.title: Lightweight Vision Transformer Compression for On-Device Plant Disease Detection in Resource-Constrained Agricultural Field Conditions
stories.author: G. Gopakumar
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of deploying high-accuracy Vision Transformers (ViTs) on resource-constrained devices.
Focuses on lightweight compression techniques specifically for on-device plant disease detection in agriculture.
Targets a critical real-world problem: improving productivity for economically significant crops like chili in resource-limited settings.

stories.title: Adaptive Gated Deepfake Detection for Low-Resolution and Resource-Constrained Environments
stories.author: Rashida Hasan
bullet_points: Introduces AdaGate-DF, a new adaptive gated framework for deepfake detection.
Addresses the limitation of existing models by optimizing for low-resolution and resource-constrained environments.
Uses image-quality cues to dynamically route samples, allowing high-quality images to exit early and save computation.

stories.title: Online Change-point Detection for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Julita Vassileva
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of non-stationarity in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) when environments change during training.
Proposes 'Patterns of Past Rewards' (PPR) as a lightweight method for online change-point detection using reward signals.
Focuses on enabling MARL agents to recognize environmental shifts proactively before attempting adaptation.

stories.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
stories.author: Benoit Corda
bullet_points: Introduces WearableQA, a new benchmark designed to test AI reasoning over longitudinal, real-world wearable data.
The benchmark utilizes complex data sources, including time series, blood biomarkers, and demographic information from 200 users.
Addresses a gap in current AI evaluation by focusing on reasoning capabilities rather than just signal processing of wearable data.

stories.title: Same Trajectory, Contradictory Rewards (ROBORMBENCH): Paraphrase Fragility in Vision Language Reward Models
stories.author: Albert No
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are being used as reward functions in robotic learning.
Current VLM reward models often lack paraphrase invariance, meaning semantically equivalent instructions yield different rewards.
This fragility can cause identical robot behaviors to be incorrectly scored as success or failure based on instruction wording.

stories.title: Multi-Step Tool-Calling over Korean Open Public APIs: A Benchmark and a Data-Synthesis Recipe
stories.author: Kyuseong Lim
bullet_points: Addresses a critical industry need: deploying on-premise, open-source LLM agents for government/public APIs due to data-sovereignty regulations.
Introduces KOPA-Bench, a new benchmark featuring 145 real-world tasks specifically designed to measure multi-step tool-calling performance in the Korean context.
Presents EDGE, a novel data synthesis method (Execution-grounded Dynamic Graph) to improve the training and evaluation of these complex LLM agent workflows.

stories.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
stories.author: Jaideep Ray
bullet_points: Investigates the critical issue of memory portability when upgrading AI models.
Identifies that simply preserving raw memory history is insufficient due to changes in model interpretation and embedding versions.
Compares different memory storage/processing methods (LC-RAW, RAG chunks, NOTES) to assess upgrade resilience.

stories.title: Large Language Models for HVAC Operations in Building Energy Systems: A Critical Review of Methods, Applications, and Deployment Readiness
stories.author: Martin Kriegel
bullet_points: The review addresses the challenge of making building automation system data actionable due to issues like heterogeneous naming and missing metadata.
It systematically analyzes 66 peer-reviewed studies focusing on applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to HVAC operations.
The research assesses these LLM applications based on evidence realism and deployment readiness across defined application and method families.

stories.title: Can Large Language Models Anticipate Behavioral Responses to Social Policies? A Case of Pension Enrollment Prediction among China's Flexible Workers
stories.author: Runhuan Feng
bullet_points: Proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) as novel tools for assessing the impact of social policies.
Introduces FlexPension-LLM, a domain-specialized LLM designed for predicting pension enrollment among flexible workers in China.
Addresses the limitations of traditional econometric methods and costly field pilot programs in policy evaluation.

stories.title: Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome Atlas
stories.author: utiiiD
bullet_points: Google DeepMind has released the AlphaGenome Atlas.
The release pertains to genomic data and AI applications.
The announcement suggests advancements in biological data processing using deep learning.

stories.title: Muse: Meta's personal AI agent, features and capabilities
stories.author: yks
bullet_points: Meta is developing a personal AI agent named Muse.
The article discusses the features and capabilities of this new agent.
This represents Meta's ongoing push into personalized AI applications.

stories.title: Benchmarking Qwen3.8 27B quantizations: 4-bit holds up, 1-bit collapses
stories.author: stared
bullet_points: The article benchmarks different quantization levels (4-bit vs. 1-bit) for the Qwen3.8 27B model.
The findings indicate that 4-bit quantization maintains performance integrity, while 1-bit quantization leads to a significant performance collapse.
This is relevant to the ongoing trend of optimizing large language models for deployment on resource-constrained hardware.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: Critiques the current implementation of 'AI Agents' in the industry.
Suggests many existing agents are functionally limited, resembling complex if-statements.
Highlights a gap between the perceived complexity of agents (planners, tools) and their actual capability.

stories.title: OpenAI Navier-Stokes Claim Signals a New Test for Multi-Agent AI Research
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: OpenAI is reportedly employing a large, coordinated group of AI agents.
The agents are being used to tackle a complex mathematical problem (Navier-Stokes equations).
This signals a potential new area of research in Multi-Agent AI systems.
